frame: After his wife went to bed he opened his laptop and started watching
name: Bare mass noun vs. article/determiner plus count noun

explanation: One side supplies a bare noun that can stand alone as the object of 'watching', while the other side supplies a determiner or quantifier that requires a following noun, or a plural count noun that is not used bare in this frame.

frame: After the third month without pay, she walked into the manager's office and
name: Speech-act vs. physical/confrontational action
reading: After three months without pay, she entered the manager's office and did something—either speaking or acting—in response to the unpaid wages.
explanation: One group continues with verbs of conveying information or reporting (often passive or with a recipient), while the other continues with verbs of making a direct request or performing a confrontational/physical act.

frame: During the search, the guard found on him a
name: object found on a person during a search

frame: Furious about what her son had done, she got him on the phone and started to
name: Act aimed at the son versus act of expressing anger
reading: A mother, furious about something her son did, gets him on the phone and begins to do something to him.

frame: He cared for the Torah ark and

frame: He clenched his fist and

frame: He entered her

frame: He filled the offering bowls and

frame: He grabbed her by the hand and led her toward the

frame: He was written up for the third time this month, so he decided to

frame: In the living room, they held the cushions down on the couch and

frame: It was his third visa application in two years, so the Home Office decided to

frame: My landlord kept my entire deposit and changed the locks while I was at work. I should
